defects.fix: Before building, audit which A4 signals are genuinely un-served vs already enforced by the harness; reallocate effort to the truly novel ones (empty-diff-after-done, tests-edited-same-turn).

verdicts.verdict: Solid on the headline primitive facts (the /rewind bash blind spot is real and well-pinned, and the Task-timeout pain is verified against live GitHub issues #49150/#61405/#28494), but several load-bearing mechanism claims are wrong or under-specified: hooks expose no token counts and tool-hooks don't fire on pure model generation (undercuts A2's enforcement story), no hook can ABORT a hung subagent (undercuts A3's strongest cluster), edit-without-Read is already enforced natively (weakens A4), and the '5s MCP spawn timeout' appears fabricated. Proceed only after the mechanism corrections in mustFix.
strengths: A1 is correct and the single best-grounded claim: /rewind checkpoints only track Write/Edit/NotebookEdit; bash rm / git reset --hard / git clean are genuinely invisible to it. The 'bash blind spot' is a real, un-served seam, not hand-waving.

The A3 pain is verified against named, live issues (#49150 no Task timeout; #61405 12+hr hang; #28494 Windows freeze). The plan's instinct to 'reproduce the deny-bypass on a named version first' before building is methodologically sound and rare.

The plan correctly distinguishes deterministic, runtime-catchable signals from judgment-requiring ones (A4) and respects the no-Claude-at-runtime constraint throughout — it does not assume an LLM judge in the loop.

A5 correctly identifies the real failure mode of guard tools: noisy permission gates get disabled (skip-permissions / bypassPermissions), making users net LESS safe. That is an accurate read of the platform's incentive trap.
Priorities are sensibly ordered by severity x buildability, and each area names a specific primitive rather than gesturing at 'use hooks'.
mustFix: A2: Correct the enforcement model. Hook input provides transcript_path but NO token counts (confirmed in docs) — you must parse usage fields out of the JSONL yourself. More importantly, PreToolUse/PostToolUse fire ONLY around tool calls, not around the model's own generation; a runaway loop that burns tokens on thinking/text with few tool calls is invisible to tool hooks. State that enforcement is per-tool-call granularity and that pure-generation runaways need a different surface (e.g. Stop/PostToolBatch + JSONL polling), or the 'halt a runaway loop' claim is unsupported.

A3: Separate PREVENT from ABORT. There is NO hook that aborts an already-running/hung subagent — which is exactly the #49150 failure mode. SubagentStart cannot block; SubagentStop/TaskCompleted only fire after the subagent returns (a hung one never does). A max-DEPTH gate IS buildable on TaskCreated (it can block creation), but the timeout/abort capability the issues actually demand cannot be delivered by any current hook. Rewrite A3 to claim only what the primitives allow, or scope it to depth-limiting + external watchdog process.

A6: Remove or source the 'Windows/WSL 5s MCP spawn timeout.' It did not verify; documented/observed MCP startup timeouts are ~30s (and tool-exec ~60s), and are configurable via MCP_TIMEOUT. Replace with the correct, cited number or drop it — a fabricated constant in the 'primitive constraints' section discredits the whole bound-the-seam analysis.

defects.issue: A4 lists 'edit-without-prior-Read' as a deterministic dishonesty signal to catch, but Claude Code ALREADY enforces read-before-edit at the tool level (Edit/Write reject if the file wasn't Read in-session). This signal is largely pre-solved by the platform, so a tool built to detect it is redundant.
defects.fix: Drop edit-without-Read from the catchable list (or note it is already enforced and only relevant for the Write-overwrite-of-unread edge case). Keep the genuinely un-served signals: empty-diff-after-'done', tests-edited-same-turn-as-claimed-pass, wrong-branch-push. Those are not natively gated.

defects.issue: A2 assumes 'local token data' exists per-tool to enforce a spend ceiling, but token usage in the JSONL is per-assistant-message (API response), not per-tool-call, and is only written after each turn — so enforcement lags by at least one model round-trip. A PreToolUse hook sees the PREVIOUS turn's usage at best.
defects.fix: Acknowledge the one-turn enforcement lag explicitly. Frame the ceiling as 'halt before the NEXT expensive turn' not 'prevent this token spend.' Validate by reading an actual JSONL and confirming where/when usage.input_tokens/output_tokens land relative to hook firing.

defects.issue: The plan treats PostToolUse as a potential enforcement point in places ('PostToolUse cannot un-rm' is acknowledged in A6, good), but A1's framing of 'PreToolUse-deny vs pre-bash-snapshot' undersells that a pre-bash snapshot hook must itself shell out (cp/git stash) on EVERY Bash call, which is exactly the kind of latency/noise A5 warns kills tools.
defects.fix: Reconcile A1 and A5: a snapshot-on-every-bash design conflicts with the 'near-zero-friction / silent-on-safe' mandate. Specify the trigger heuristic (snapshot only when the command matches a destructive-pattern allowlist: rm, git reset --hard, git clean, mv, truncate, >) so it stays silent on safe bash.

defects.issue: A3 references a 'QUARANTINED Bash-deny bypass' as unverified and rightly flags reproduce-first, but does not state what 'named version' means operationally — Claude Code versions move fast and bypass behaviors are patched, so a bypass found on one build may be gone by build time.
defects.fix: Pin the exact version string (claude --version) in the repro, and add a check that the bypass still reproduces on the CURRENT stable before designing any mitigation around it. Treat a non-reproducing bypass as out-of-scope, not as a feature gap.

bullshitFlags: 'Windows/WSL 5s MCP spawn timeout' (A6) — specific constant that did not verify against docs or issues; documented timeouts are ~30s startup / ~60s exec and MCP_TIMEOUT-configurable. Reads as fabricated precision.

A2's 'halt a runaway loop' — overclaims hook capability. Tool hooks cannot see or interrupt pure-generation loops with no tool calls, and carry no live token counts. The enforcement primitive is weaker than implied.

A3's framing that a 'hook surface imposes ... a Task() timeout/abort that Claude Code lacks' — implies a hook CAN provide the abort. No current hook aborts a running/hung subagent; this is the one thing the cited issues prove is impossible today. Conflates depth-limiting (buildable) with abort (not buildable via hooks).
A4 listing edit-without-prior-Read as a dishonesty signal to build for — the platform already enforces this; presenting it as an open seam is an unsupported assumption about Claude Code's tool layer.
'native checkpointing does NOT track bash-modified files' (A1) — this one is NOT bullshit (verified true), flagged here only to record it was checked and confirmed, not assumed.

verdicts.verdict: This plan picks REAL, frequent, painful problems — I verified the four load-bearing claims against live evidence and they hold: /rewind genuinely ignores bash-modified files (Anthropic's own checkpointing docs confirm rm/mv/git reset are not tracked → A1's seam is real); issue #49150 "Task tool has no timeout" is real and accurately summarized, and #68619 confirms catastrophic recursive fan-out burning 1.2M tokens in 30 min (A3 is the strongest cluster, correctly identified); permission fatigue → skip-permissions is real, with Anthropic's own data showing users approve 93% of prompts blind and a documented `rm ~/` home-dir wipe (A5). This is NOT a solution in search of a problem — the pains are severe and hook-buildable, and the plan's instinct to chase "the un-served seam" rather than re-display known data is correct. The score is capped at 7, not higher, for three product-grade defects. (1) The provenance of the pain taxonomy is unverifiable from the repo: tribunal/ contains ONLY a README claiming "~1000 real complaints → validated taxonomy → structured deep-dive," but NONE of PP-01..PP-16, the taxonomy, or the deep-dive exist on disk — the only actual evidence base is the SIBLING product swarmloop's RESEARCH.md, which itself admits its method is "a focused sample... not a scrape of thousands." So the plan's repeated word "verified" is, as written, an unbacked assertion — the findings happen to be true, but the plan can't show its work. (2) A5 — the single most adoption-relevant area, because noisy gates are what drive disablement — has ALREADY been shipped by Anthropic as "Auto mode" (a classifier that is silent-on-safe, loud-on-irreversible, exactly the plan's stated design). That is not a coincidence to gloss over; it is the incumbent eating the seam, and A6 (the moat question) never names it. (3) A4's dishonesty signals risk being annoying-on-safe (edit-without-prior-Read and empty-diff-after-done fire constantly in legitimate workflows), which by the plan's OWN A5 thesis will get the tool disabled. Adoption friction, not detection cleverness, is the real risk and it is under-weighted.
strengths: Problem selection is excellent and evidence-true: I independently confirmed A1 (rewind blind to bash), A3 (#49150 no Task timeout + #68619 recursive token burn), and A5 (93%-approve-blind fatigue, real rm ~/ disaster). These are frequent, severe, money/data-losing pains — the opposite of a vitamin.

Correctly distinguishes the SEAM from the displayed problem: 'incumbent monitors are post-hoc read-only; the seam is enforcement+prediction, not display' (A2) and 'native checkpointing does NOT track bash → that blind spot is the un-served seam' (A1) is exactly the right product instinct in a crowded space.

Intellectually honest about its own weak spots: explicitly QUARANTINES the deny-bypass as 'unverified, reproduce first' (A3) and partitions catchable-from-uncatchable dishonesty (A4) instead of overclaiming a magic lie-detector. This restraint is rare and credible.
A6 names the right primitive constraints (PostToolUse cannot un-rm; Windows/WSL 5s MCP spawn timeout) — design respects real Claude Code capabilities rather than wishing for hooks that don't exist.
Priority ordering is defensible: PP-07/PP-01/PP-08 (data loss, spend, runaway) are genuinely the highest-pain, highest-frequency clusters; leading with them is the user-right call.

defects.issue: The word 'verified' is load-bearing across every area but the verification artifact is absent from the repo. tribunal/ is a README only; the PP taxonomy, the ~1000 complaints, and the 'structured deep-dive' are not on disk. The closest real evidence (swarmloop/docs/RESEARCH.md) self-describes as a non-exhaustive sample. A reviewer cannot trace any PP-code to a source.
defects.fix: Before proceeding, commit the actual evidence: a PP-01..PP-16 table where each pain row carries >=2 concrete citations (issue # or dated post URL) and a frequency proxy (issue reactions / thread count). Replace bare 'verified' with the citation. If the taxonomy lives elsewhere, link it from tribunal/ — do not let the plan reference evidence that isn't checkable.

defects.issue: A5's design (silent-on-safe, loud-on-irreversible to REMOVE net prompts) is already shipped by Anthropic as 'Auto mode' — a classifier doing precisely this. The plan treats permission fatigue as an open seam when the platform is actively closing it. This is the highest redundant-guard risk in the whole plan and it is invisible in the plan text.
defects.fix: Rewrite A5 to start from 'Auto mode exists — what does it NOT cover?' (e.g. bash destruction classification, project-specific irreversibility, offline/no-classifier determinism) and either find the residual seam or DROP A5 and reallocate priority. Do not build a second prompt-classifier next to Anthropic's.

defects.issue: A4's deterministic signals (edit-without-prior-Read, empty-diff-after-done, tests-edited-same-turn) have high false-positive rates in legitimate flows: agents legitimately edit files they saw in a prior session, finish turns with no diff (analysis-only), and edit tests in the same turn as fixing test infra. By the plan's own A5 thesis, a noisy honesty-checker gets disabled.
defects.fix: For each A4 signal, specify the expected false-positive workflow and a suppression rule, and define the signal as 'flag, never block' with a measured precision target (e.g. >0.8 on a labeled session corpus) BEFORE it ships. Make A4 produce an end-of-turn digest, not an inline interruption.

defects.issue: A6 (the moat/distribution question) is correctly listed but starved at priority 6 and scoped only to 'the chosen pain' — i.e. it runs AFTER the build direction is effectively locked by A1-A5. For a User Advocate, 'will anyone install this over the native feature / a competing hook pack' is a gating question, not a closing one.
defects.fix: Promote a lightweight incumbent-map (native feature + top 2 community hook packs per pain, with their exact gap) to run alongside A1, so each area inherits a one-line 'why us, not the platform' before any hook is written. Kill any area whose seam the platform already owns.

defects.issue: No area asks WHO the user is or how they'd discover/adopt this. A spend-ceiling hook (A2) and a runaway-killer (A3) serve power users on Max plans running unattended loops — a real but narrow segment. The plan never states the target user, install friction (it's a hook pack → manual settings.json edit), or the trigger moment for adoption.
defects.fix: Add a one-paragraph user definition + adoption path: who hits PP-01/07/08 often enough to install a guard, how they find it, and what the zero-config install is. Near-zero friction is asserted in A6's rationale but never operationalized.

bullshitFlags: 'Severe, verified, hook-buildable pains' (rationale) and 'most actionable finding' / 'strongest verified cluster' (A1/A3): the pains ARE true, but 'verified' overclaims relative to what's on disk — there is no traceable verification artifact in tribunal/. The evidence that does exist (swarmloop RESEARCH.md) explicitly disclaims being exhaustive. Calling it 'verified' without showing the citations is the exact false-confidence tribunal is supposed to catch.

A5 implicitly assumes permission fatigue is an UNADDRESSED design space ('what design adds protection while REMOVING net prompts'). Wrong assumption about the current Claude Code platform: Anthropic shipped Auto mode doing exactly silent-on-safe/loud-on-irreversible. The plan reasons as if the incumbent doesn't exist.

'218-agent fan-outs, zero output' (A3) is stated as a specific verified figure but no source is attached in-plan; the real, citable artifacts are #49150 and #68619 (1000-agent cap, 1.2M tokens/30min). The number may be real but is presented with more precision than its in-plan backing supports — attach the issue # or soften it.

Near-zero-friction distribution ('be near-zero-friction, or die in obscurity', A6 rationale) is asserted as a design value but the deliverable is a hooks/settings.json pack, which is NOT near-zero-friction to install for the fatigued, non-power user the plan elsewhere worries about. Unexamined tension between the friction claim and the chosen distribution form.
mustFix: Produce the traceable evidence base before building: a PP-01..PP-16 table, each pain with >=2 dated citations (issue #/URL) + a frequency proxy, committed into tribunal/. Replace every bare 'verified' with its citation. Without this, the plan's central premise is unfalsifiable.

Resolve the A5-vs-Anthropic-Auto-mode collision: re-anchor A5 on the residual gap Auto mode does NOT cover, or drop A5 and reallocate. Do not greenlight building a second safe-permissions classifier next to the platform's.

Add an incumbent + adoption map (native feature, top community hook packs, exact gap, target user, zero-config install path) as a gate that EACH area must pass before a hook is written — pull the A6 moat question forward instead of running it last.

verdicts.verdict: The code-grounded half of this work is unusually honest and survives adversarial verification — I independently confirmed the load-bearing claims about engine-light.ts (demote(), cleanCitations slice-without-dedupe, last_verified=today leak) and engine-proxy.ts (keyedFetch has a private AbortController and no signal param, making every parent watchdog provably inert). Those are real, checkable, and correctly diagnosed. The weakness is the entire external-evidence layer: ~9 arXiv citations carry YYMM IDs (2603–2605 = 2026 papers) and specific quantitative claims (53ms/76ms gate latency, 100%→25%→0% hallucination, 36.8% bypass, 81% FNR, 10.7% vs 4.8% URL hallucination) hang off papers I cannot resolve and that are exactly the fabrication-prone artifact the findings themselves warn about. The work partially inoculates itself with a candid gaps section, but several numbers are stated in the body with more confidence than the gaps admit. Net: trustworthy engineering diagnosis, unverified literature scaffolding. Proceed, but treat every external statistic as unconfirmed until a URL resolves.
strengths: Code claims are precise and verifiable. I confirmed keyedFetch(service,path,payload) at engine-proxy.ts:118 has NO signal/opts param and creates its own AbortController at :127 with a 28s timer at :128 — the 'inert watchdog' diagnosis is structurally correct, not hand-waving. A parent budget genuinely cannot abort the leaf.

The A4 'count != independence' claim is real: cleanCitations (engine-light.ts:235-241) filters only by valid.has(x) then slice(0,4) with zero domain/publisher dedupe, so 4 citations to one syndicated wire pass any count threshold. Verified against source, not asserted.

The 'fake-freshness' leak is real and load-bearing: last_verified: this.today (engine-light.ts:166) stamps today regardless of source publish date, and it ties cleanly to the independently-logged defects (Jun26 dates, 0-verified). The finding connects code to observed failure.

demote() (engine-light.ts:226-230) is exactly as described: codomain is strictly {single, inferred}, so the live engine structurally cannot emit verified-check. The A4 recommendation ('keep check unreachable and SAY SO') follows correctly from verified behavior.

The gaps section is genuinely adversarial against the authors' own conclusions — it concedes no published eval tests a provenance gate inside a self-critiquing tribunal loop, that the 0% figure is n=8, that the ~8.3% overhead is attached to two different mechanisms, and that fail-open vs fail-closed has no head-to-head on research-claim shipping. This is the opposite of overclaiming.

Build-time-lint recommendations (confidence==='single' => citations.length>=1) are deterministic, model-free, and would catch the alleged curated-layer contradictions without trusting any LLM — a proposal whose correctness does not depend on the unverified citations.
mustFix: Resolve or quarantine every arXiv citation before any number derived from it ships in a deliverable. The IDs (2603.20953, 2511.05524, 2604.03173, 2604.04978, 2604.13536, 2602.18693, 2605.06635, 2509.11851, 2407.11843) are unverified and use a 2026 YYMM scheme; the findings' OWN cited 10.7% deep-research-agent URL-hallucination rate applies to this very output. Until each URL resolves AND a span-match confirms it supports the attached statistic, mark every external number as ? (inferred), not as fact.

Verify the curated-layer contradiction claim (category-regime.ts:571-572 'confidence:single, citations:[]') against the ACTUAL HEAD before acting on it. I could not find category-regime.ts or competitor-verify.ts in the copies on disk (mc_v8 is an older single-Promise.all variant); the cited line numbers correspond to a tree I cannot see. Confirm the file/lines exist as quoted, or downgrade A4's 'curated bypass' from a verified defect to an unverified hypothesis.

Reconcile the line-number drift. Findings cite engine-light.ts:281-292 as the groundedness gate, but in the on-disk copy that gate is at :219-230 and :281-292 is exhibit-shaper code. The substance is right but the coordinates are stale — pin every code citation to a specific commit SHA so reviewers aren't chasing the wrong lines.
bullshitFlags: OVERCLAIM via false precision: '53ms median / 76ms p99, N=1,000' and '7/8 verified, 1/8 blocked, 0% hallucination' are stated as hard measurements but sourced entirely to unresolvable 2026-dated arXiv IDs. Specific decimals borrowed from a possibly-fabricated source are MORE dangerous than a vague claim, because they read as rigor.

HAND-WAVING on the overhead figure: '~8.3% overhead' / '~8%' is quoted as if settled, while the gaps section quietly admits the figure 'appears attached to two different mechanisms across papers — treat as soft.' The body and the caveat contradict each other on the same number; the body wins by default in a skim.

SELF-UNDERMINING citation: the work cites a deep-research-agent citation-hallucination rate (10.7% URLs never existed; one flagship agent 13.3%) WHILE BEING a deep-research output whose own citations I cannot resolve. Either the rate applies to this document (so its citations are suspect) or it is special-pleading that this agent is the exception — unsupported either way.

UNSUPPORTED quantitative leap in platform-fit: '~20B/yr default search', '~26B total to partners in 2021', 'slotting ~5k-50k/SKU/chain, endcap up to ~75k', '<25% of a category open', 'Mozilla ~6M selections' are presented as facts but flagged in gaps as 'litigation-era', 'unaudited industry ranges', and 'an engagement, not share, metric'. The body asserts; the gaps retract. The numbers should not appear in the body without the retraction attached.

ASSUMPTION-AS-FACT about Claude Code internals: the A1 finding states file checkpointing 'explicitly does NOT capture Bash-mediated changes' and quotes a docs URL plus GitHub issue #14002 (0-file snapshots) as verbatim — I cannot verify either the quote or the issue number. The architectural recommendation (PreToolUse/Bash hook, fail-closed) is sound regardless, but the specific vendor-concession quote and issue number are unverified and load-bearing for the 'vendor-conceded seam' framing.

INFERENCE dressed as verification in A2: 'best-achievable halt freshness is ~60s' and 'LULD Limit State -> 5-min pause after 15s' are presented confidently, yet gaps admits the RSS field schema could not be confirmed, the 60s is 'a stated tier delay' not a measured end-to-end lag, and it is unconfirmed whether intraday halt state is even needed vs an at-open snapshot. The certainty in the finding outruns the evidence in the gap.

defects.issue: Every external quantitative claim depends on arXiv IDs that cannot be resolved offline and use a 2026 YYMM scheme (2603-2605). This is the single highest-risk surface and the findings stake specific numbers on it.
defects.fix: Before next phase, run each ID through a resolver. For any that 404 or whose abstract does not contain the quoted statistic, strike the number from the body and move it to gaps as 'claim could not be sourced'. Do not let a single unresolved citation back a body-level statistic.

defects.issue: Code citations point at line numbers that do not match the copies on disk (engine-light gate is at 219-230, not 281-292; backbone has one Promise.all not two at 306/325; competitor-verify.ts and category-regime.ts absent from the verifiable copies).
defects.fix: Pin the review to a single commit SHA and re-quote all line numbers from it. Explicitly confirm competitor-verify.ts:398-417 and category-regime.ts:571-572 exist as cited, or downgrade those specific findings to unverified.

defects.issue: Fail-open vs fail-closed recommendation (A0) leans on a 0%-false-claim result that the gaps concede is n=8 and from a different domain (code-execution / tool-auth, not free-text research claims). The body recommends gating high-harm classes fail-closed partly on this thin base.
defects.fix: Reframe the fail-closed recommendation as a hypothesis to be A/B-tested on the tribunal's OWN corpus with block-rate and FPR instrumented, not as an evidence-backed default. Set the over-block alarm threshold before flipping any class to fail-closed.

defects.issue: Platform-fit 'Incumbent Gate' numbers (20B, 26B, slotting ranges, Mozilla 6M) appear in the body as facts but are retracted in gaps as litigation-era / unaudited / wrong-metric.
defects.fix: Move all such figures behind a recency-flagged, dated, runtime-curated tile and never render them as point estimates — model as wide ranges with an explicit 'unaudited industry range' annotation, exactly as the finding's own implication says but the body does not do.

defects.issue: A2 confidence ('60s stale by design', '15s->pause') outruns its evidence: RSS field schema unconfirmed, 60s is a stated tier not a measured lag, and the need for intraday halt state at all is unconfirmed.
defects.fix: Before building A2, fetch one live Nasdaq Trade Halt RSS sample and confirm (a) the field schema and (b) measured feed lag. Resolve the at-open-vs-intraday question first — if at-open-only, most of A2's freshness analysis is moot.

verdicts.verdict: Strong, code-grounded findings with one architecturally dangerous conflation. I independently verified the load-bearing code claims: demote()'s codomain is exactly {single,inferred} (engine-light.ts:288-291), cleanCitations slices to 4 with zero domain dedupe (:303-309), keyedFetch has a private 28s controller and no signal param (engine-proxy.ts:118-128), research-backbone fans out two bare Promise.all batches with no shared signal (:306,:325), verifyCompetitorEntities uses the leaky Promise.race([run(),setTimeout]) where run() is not aborted on budget-win (competitor-verify.ts:411-414), the A5 module-level shownReports/lastGoodReports latch and its R136 remount comment exist as described (report.$reportId.tsx:204-227), and the A4 contradiction is real — category-regime.ts:571-572 ship confidence:"single",citations:[] in direct violation of engine-light.ts:290. The runtime/product half (A3, A4, A5) is the best work here: accurate to the line, the fixes are correct and proportionate, and they earn high marks. My lens is Claude Code technical soundness, and that is exactly where the findings are weakest. A0 and A1 are framed as Claude Code agent-safety primitives ("before the agent ships/acts", "PreToolUse/Bash hook", "dual gate") but the entire evidence base and every cited code analog is the PRODUCT RUNTIME (TypeScript engine, Cloudflare SSR, SQL triggers, the _verify CI harness in Downloads/mc-analyze) — none of which is Claude Code. The findings repeatedly say "generalize engine-light demote() into A0" while also saying A0 gates "every shippable assertion / 'done' message" by the agent: those are two different machines in two different runtimes, and merging them is a category error that will produce an unbuildable spec. Separately, the A1 PreToolUse/Bash hook design has real Claude Code footguns the findings acknowledge but under-weight (script-wrapped bypass, glob/var resolution, Windows-first cross-platform, fail-closed deadlock risk). Net: excellent diagnosis of the product, shaky on the Claude Code mechanics it claims as the architectural slot. Proceed, but only after A0/A1 are de-conflated and the hook design is reality-checked against actual Claude Code hook behavior.
strengths: Code claims are independently verifiable and accurate to the exact line. I checked the seven most load-bearing ones (demote codomain, cleanCitations slice-no-dedupe, keyedFetch private controller, two bare Promise.all batches, the Promise.race leak, the A5 module latch + R136 comment, the category-regime single+empty-citations contradiction) and every one matched. This is rare and raises trust in the rest.

A3 root-cause is correct and the fix is the right shape: thread a signal through keyedFetch (add opts?:{signal}), one shared AbortController + aggregate budget in runResearchBackbone, and replace the Promise.race wait-stopper with an AbortController whose abort is also handed to every leaf. The 'inert watchdog' framing (higher timers can't cancel a leaf that owns a private controller) is exactly right, and AbortSignal.any is genuinely available in workerd. Proportionate: explicitly rejects pulling in p-limit/semaphore deps.

A4 is the standout. Recompute-confidence-as-a-pure-function-with-zero-trusted-inputs is the correct invariant, the distinct-domains-not-raw-ids point is a real exploitable gap (3 cites to one syndicated wire clears any count threshold), and the last_verified=today fake-freshness leak is a concrete shipped defect that maps to the logged 'Jun26 dates' incident. The proposed build-time lint (single ⇒ citations.length≥1) catches an existing in-repo contradiction with no model in the loop — high-value, low-cost, and it slots into the existing _verify harness.

A5 correctly distinguishes the within-mount flicker guard (placeholderData, never persisted) from the cross-remount latch (module Set/Map), and is intellectually honest about re-scoping from 'the recorded blank (fixed)' to two genuinely-uncovered residual seams (scroll-restoration jump, cold-realm partitioned-iframe reload). It even flags that the R136 comment mis-attributes the remount to ?fresh-strip — a real bug in the team's own mental model.

Intellectual honesty throughout the gaps section: it concedes the 0% dual-gate result is n=8, that fail-open vs fail-closed has no head-to-head on research claims, that the ~8ms gate latency is for cheap policy checks not the NLI/independence-clustering the tribunal actually needs, and that resolvability ≠ support. A reviewer who pre-discloses their own weakest evidence is easier to trust on the rest.
mustFix: DE-CONFLATE A0. The findings fuse two different machines in two different runtimes: (1) the product runtime gate that grades the GENERATED REPORT (engine-light demote(), SQL fabrication_law, the _verify CI harness) and (2) a Claude Code AGENT gate that catches the agent's own 'done'/overclaim. 'Generalize demote() into A0' and 'A0 gates every shippable assertion/done message the agent emits' cannot both be one component — one is a TS function in a Cloudflare worker, the other would have to be a PreToolUse/Stop hook in Claude Code with access to the agent's tool stream. Before phase 2, split A0 into A0-runtime (the report gate, already 80% built — verified) and A0-agent (the Claude Code tribunal gate, NOT built and NOT analogous to demote). Otherwise the spec is unbuildable.

REALITY-CHECK A1 AGAINST ACTUAL CLAUDE CODE HOOK BEHAVIOR before building. The findings concede 'scripts written to disk bypass hook interception' and 'PreToolUse sees only the top-level string' but then still propose a synchronous fail-CLOSED snapshot hook as v1. On the user's Windows-primary box this is a minefield: (a) PreToolUse(Bash) gives you the command string but resolving rm globs / variable expansion / sed -i targets correctly enough to snapshot the RIGHT bytes is the unsolved part the findings admit, so fail-closed-on-snapshot-failure will deadlock the agent on every command it can't statically resolve; (b) the existing project hook is PostToolUse with a 5s timeout — a synchronous pre-bash byte-copy with verify-before-proceed adds latency to EVERY destructive command and the 600s ceiling is per-hook not per-session. Require a measured reflink/hardlink latency number and an explicit fallback (downgrade to 'ask', never silent fail-open) documented before A1 is greenlit.

A0's deterministic provenance check needs its actual cost measured, not assumed. The cited 8-76ms is for cheap policy/ACL checks. The tribunal's real check is URL resolution at scale + span-match + (per the design) NLI/HHEM entailment + independence clustering — that is seconds-to-minutes and network-dependent, and on the agent's OWN deep-research output (which the findings correctly flag as the highest-risk input). Putting that synchronously in front of every critical claim will either blow the latency budget or get sampled down to the point it stops being a gate. The phase gate must include a measured end-to-end provenance-check latency on a real corpus and a sync/async split decision, or A0 is theater.

defects.issue: A0 conflates the product runtime gate (engine-light demote(), SQL fabrication_law, the _verify CI harness — all in Cloudflare/Deno/CI, none in Claude Code) with a Claude Code agent gate that catches the agent's own 'done'/overclaim. The finding says both 'generalize demote() into A0' AND 'A0 binds to every shippable assertion / file write / done message' (an agent-level interception). These are two machines in two runtimes and cannot be one component.
defects.fix: Split into A0-runtime (report-artifact gate, mostly built) and A0-agent (a Claude Code Stop/PreToolUse-level check on the agent's claims). Specify each against its real runtime; do not reuse demote() as the agent gate — it has no access to the agent's tool stream.

defects.issue: A1 specifies a synchronous fail-CLOSED PreToolUse/Bash snapshot hook as v1, but the same finding admits PreToolUse sees only the top-level command string and script-wrapped/glob/variable-expanded destructive commands bypass it. Fail-closed on a command whose targets can't be statically resolved deadlocks the agent; the user is Windows-primary where rm/trash/reflink semantics differ from the macOS analogs cited.
defects.fix: Make v1 effect-based but DOWNGRADE-not-deadlock: on unresolvable/script-wrapped targets escalate to 'ask' (never silent fail-open, never hard deny-all). Measure reflink/hardlink latency on Windows (ReFS/dev-drive vs NTFS — reflink is not universally available on NTFS). Drop the 'fully reversible' framing entirely.

defects.issue: The ~8ms / 53ms-median gate-latency numbers are cited as if they bound A0, but they are for cheap deterministic policy/ACL checks. The provenance checks A0 actually needs (URL resolution, span-match, NLI/HHEM entailment, MinHash independence clustering, on agent-produced research URLs) are orders of magnitude slower and network-bound. The finding flags this in gaps but the design implications still imply a synchronous per-critical-claim gate at ~8% overhead.
defects.fix: Require a measured end-to-end provenance-check latency on the tribunal's own corpus before locking thresholds. Mandate a sync/async split: cheap checks (URL resolves, hash/span match) synchronous; expensive checks (entailment, clustering) async in the post-build gate or a sampled auditor. State the real overhead, not the borrowed 8%.

defects.issue: The A0 'critical-claim predicate fires only on critical actions → ~8% overhead, +20% Macro-F1' borrows InferAct's numbers (a web-agent buy-now misalignment benchmark) and EviBound's 8.3% (code-execution artifacts) and applies them to free-text research-claim shipping. The finding's own gaps concede no published gate runs inside a self-critiquing tribunal where the same model family produces and partly judges the claim — so generalization is inferred, not measured.
defects.fix: Label these as analogical priors, not predicted operating points. Instrument block-rate and FPR from day one on the tribunal's real traffic and treat the cited percentages as hypotheses to validate, not targets to design to.

defects.issue: A0/A4 lean on 'recompute as a pure function, never trust the model's verbalized confidence' as the universal fix, but the most fabrication-prone check (does the source actually SUPPORT the claim) is itself an LLM/NLI judgment. The finding acknowledges resolvability ≠ support but the design still routes 'source supports claim' as one of three 'deterministic predicates'. Entailment is not deterministic; calling it so smuggles a model back into the trusted path the design claims to eliminate.
defects.fix: Rename that predicate honestly (e.g. 'entailment-scored, thresholded') and treat it as a probabilistic input gated by a deterministic threshold, with the threshold benchmarked on the corpus. Keep only URL-resolves and recency/independence as truly deterministic.

defects.issue: A5 proposes a regression test asserting 'once everShown, no skeleton/progress/error return is reachable for any isLoading/isFetching/isError/enriching combination', but the _verify harness runs in a separate copied environment (Downloads/mc-analyze) under jsdom — module-level latch state (shownReports Set) persists across tests in a single process and can mask or fake-pass the invariant if not reset per-test.
defects.fix: Reset the module latch (clear shownReports/lastGoodReports) in a beforeEach, and assert the invariant via fresh module imports or an injectable latch, so the test proves the guarantee rather than inheriting prior-test state.

defects.issue: A2's '60s halt freshness' rests on the Nasdaq RSS tier-delay figure, but the finding's gaps admit the actual feed field schema (machine-readable resumption timestamp/reason vs HTML-only) and real end-to-end lag distribution are unconfirmed. Building a 'is this name paused?' indicator on an unverified field contract risks shipping an indicator that can't actually parse resumption.
defects.fix: Confirm the RSS body schema (fetch one sample, inspect fields) before committing to any resumption/threshold rendering; if HTML-only, scope A2 to a binary paused/not-paused flag and drop resumption-time claims.

bullshitFlags: A0/A1 are framed as the 'architecturally correct layer 2 of the agent-safety stack' for a CLAUDE CODE agent, but every piece of supporting code evidence (engine-light, SQL triggers, the _verify harness) is the PRODUCT RUNTIME, which is not Claude Code. The 'generalize demote() into A0' instruction is the tell: demote() grades a generated report in a Cloudflare worker and has no relationship to intercepting the agent's own tool calls. The architectural-slot claim is borrowed from the product gate and re-pointed at the agent without bridging the runtime gap.

'53ms median / 76ms p99' and '~8.3% overhead' are stated with false precision relative to what A0 must actually do. Those numbers are from OAP policy-ACL checks and EviBound code-artifact verification respectively; the finding even admits in gaps they're 'for cheap policy checks only' and 'attached to two different mechanisms across papers — treat as soft.' Quoting them in the headline findings as if they characterize the tribunal's provenance gate is overclaiming.

'Snapshot exactly the bytes Edit/Write checkpointing cannot see ... FAIL CLOSED on snapshot failure' is presented as a clean interception point, but the same finding concedes scripts-to-disk and globs/variable-expansion bypass the hook. A fail-closed gate that cannot resolve its own targets is not a safety mechanism, it's an agent deadlock. The 'clean, model-cooperation-free interception point' phrasing oversells a hook that is blind to exactly the destructive cases that matter most.

The n=8 EviBound '0% hallucination via dual gate' is cited three separate times as the load-bearing justification for the dual-gate architecture, with the n=8 caveat buried. Eight tasks on code-execution artifacts is a suggestive pilot, not evidence that a dual gate drives research-claim fabrication to zero. The repetition manufactures more confidence than the single small study supports.

'Resumption is rendered as estimate ~5 min pending auction + new bands' (A2) and the precise LULD band-doubling 9:30-9:45 calibration are stated as build-ready, but gaps admit it's unconfirmed whether the tool even needs intraday halt state vs an at-open snapshot — in which case the entire 60s-lag and band-doubling apparatus is moot. The finding designs a real-time mechanism for a requirement it hasn't confirmed exists.

verdicts.verdict: On the dimension I own — correctness of claims about Claude Code primitives (hooks, checkpointing, the Task/subagent tribunal, MCP, settings, limits) — this dossier is unusually well-grounded. I independently verified the four load-bearing platform assertions against official docs and GitHub and every one checked out verbatim: (1) file checkpointing tracks ONLY Write/Edit/NotebookEdit and explicitly excludes Bash-mediated changes, plus directory create/move/delete is not undone (confirmed at code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing, Warning + Limitations table); (2) PreToolUse(Bash) receives tool_input.command + cwd pre-execution, returns allow/deny/ask, has a 600s default timeout, and supports updatedInput rewriting (confirmed at /docs/en/hooks); (3) GitHub #14002's 0-file-snapshot race is real — and the search surfaced #34368 'Rewind offers to undo file deletions it cannot actually restore', which CORROBORATES A1 more strongly than the dossier itself claims; (4) destructive_command_guard fails open, creates no backups, and concedes scripts-written-to-disk bypass interception. The architectural instinct is correct on the primitives that matter: a PreToolUse/Bash hook IS the only model-cooperation-free, synchronous interception point, capture-before-proceed IS necessary because the native checkpoint race creates 0-file snapshots, and fail-closed-on-snapshot-failure is the right inversion of the existing guard tools. I am withholding 2 points because the dossier repeatedly imports academic-paper claims about a 'self-critiquing tribunal' loop and maps them onto Claude Code's Task/subagent mechanism WITHOUT verifying how that mechanism actually behaves — and a few of those mappings rest on platform assumptions that are wrong or unstated (see defects). The dossier's own gaps section honestly flags the biggest one (no published eval tests a provenance gate inside a same-model-family tribunal), which I credit.
strengths: Every concrete Claude Code primitive claim I could check is correct and precisely worded. The file-checkpointing exclusions (Bash changes untracked; directory create/move/delete not undone; local files only) match the official Warning + Limitations table verbatim — this is the architectural seam A1 is built on and it is real, not assumed.

PreToolUse(Bash) capabilities are stated correctly down to the detail: receives the command string + cwd before execution, can allow/deny/ask/defer via hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision, 600s default timeout, and updatedInput rewriting. The A1 'synchronous, capture-then-verify-then-run, fail-closed' design is implementable exactly as described because hooks are synchronous by default (async is an explicit opt-in feature in the reference).

The coverage-not-accuracy thesis (A0: gate the artifact boundary, not one chokepoint; 36.8% bypass via in-project edits) is the single most important and correct platform insight in the dossier. It correctly recognizes that Claude Code has MULTIPLE state-change paths (Bash, Edit/Write, the final assistant 'done' message) and that gating publish-only is theater — this matches how the tool actually routes side effects.

A1's 'scripts written to disk bypass interception' is verified true and load-bearing: PreToolUse sees only the top-level tool_input.command, so `bash ./cleanup.sh` shows the hook a string that reveals nothing about the rm inside. The dossier correctly escalates this to a coarser net (snapshot cwd subtree / downgrade to ask) rather than over-promising 'fully reversible' — exactly the right honesty given the primitive's limits.

The cross-cutting invariant (trust signal = recomputed pure function over a provenance object, never a stored/model-emitted opinion, enforced at code/DB-constraint level so the judged agent cannot argue past it) is the correct response to the fact that a subagent in a Task loop CAN re-litigate any in-context instruction but CANNOT defeat a deterministic gate outside its context window. This is a correct and sophisticated reading of the subagent threat model.
mustFix: A0/cross-cutting: State explicitly where the 'tribunal' provenance gate physically runs relative to the judged subagent, because the whole 'agent cannot argue past it' guarantee depends on it. A subagent spawned via the Task tool returns a SINGLE final text result to the orchestrator and shares NO tool-call transcript or memory with it; the gate must run in the orchestrator (or a hook/DB constraint), NEVER as an instruction inside the judged subagent's own prompt — otherwise it is exactly the 'LLM grading its own homework' the dossier warns against. Name the execution locus (PreToolUse hook / orchestrator post-processing / SQL trigger) for BOTH A0 gates.

A0 'bind the gate to every ship/state-change path': enumerate the ACTUAL Claude Code exit paths, not an abstract set. At minimum: Bash (PreToolUse/Bash hook), Edit/Write/NotebookEdit (PreToolUse with those matchers OR PostToolUse), MCP tool calls (matcher mcp__<server>__<tool>), and the final assistant message itself — which NO PreToolUse hook can see because emitting text is not a tool call. The 'done/overclaim' failure mode the dossier centers on exits via that last path; A0 must specify a Stop/SubagentStop hook or orchestrator-side check for it, or the dual gate has a hole on its primary target.

A1: drop or heavily caveat any cross-platform claim that the same PreToolUse/Bash shape covers the user's Windows/PowerShell environment. The destructive-command SHAPES listed (rm, sed -i, find -delete, dd, git reset --hard) are POSIX; on this user's primary Windows/PowerShell setup the tool_input.command is PowerShell (Remove-Item, Set-Content, rm as an alias), and reflink/hardlink copy semantics differ entirely. The hook fires either way, but the shape-matcher and the COW-copy mechanism are NOT cross-platform as written — specify per-shell shape sets and a Windows-viable snapshot (copy/VSS) or scope v1 to one platform.

defects.issue: The dossier treats EviBound/InferAct (which gate a single agent's code-execution or one tool 'Buy Now' action) and the 'tribunal' (a multi-subagent review loop over free-text research claims) as transferable, but never grounds the transfer in how Claude Code's Task/subagent mechanism actually works. Subagents do not share context with the orchestrator or each other; a 'post-build verification gate that re-checks the shipped artifact' is therefore a SEPARATE orchestrator-side step, not something a peer subagent can be trusted to do on the producer's transcript (it never sees it).
defects.fix: Reframe the dual gate in Claude Code terms: pre-build gate = a deterministic check (hook or orchestrator code) on the provenance object the producing subagent RETURNS; post-build gate = an orchestrator-side re-resolve/span-match on the final artifact bytes. Explicitly state that no subagent grades another subagent's hidden reasoning — only its returned artifact — because cross-subagent transcripts are not visible. This closes the 'same model family judges itself' gap the dossier's own gaps section flags.

defects.issue: A0 claims the gate can 'block' a 'done' overclaim, but the mechanism for intercepting the agent's final natural-language completion message is left implicit. No PreToolUse hook fires on the assistant emitting prose — only on tool calls. If the agent says 'shipped and verified' in text without a corresponding tool call, every PreToolUse-based gate is blind to it.
defects.fix: Specify a Stop / SubagentStop hook (which DOES fire when the agent finishes and can block with continue:false + a reason) or an orchestrator-side assertion over the returned result, as the enforcement point for completion/'done' claims. Without naming this, A0's headline 'catch the done/overclaim divergence' is not actually wired to a primitive that fires on that event.

defects.issue: A1 leans on AbortSignal.any/timeout in workerd and TanStack Router remountDeps/scrollRestoration semantics as load-bearing facts (A3, A5). These are Cloudflare-runtime and React-router framework claims, not Claude Code primitives, and were not verified here — they sit outside the dossier's strongest evidence base and outside my lens, yet are stated with 'high' confidence.
defects.fix: Tag A3/A5's runtime-and-framework assertions (workerd AbortSignal support date, 'search-param change does not remount without remountDeps', scrollRestoration timing) as framework-verified-separately rather than bundling them under the same confidence as the Claude-Code-primitive claims, which ARE verified. Keep the platform-primitive claims (hooks, checkpointing) at high confidence; down-rank the framework ones to 'needs runtime confirmation'.

defects.issue: The dossier cites the file-checkpointing race (#14002) as justification for synchronous capture, which is correct, but understates the strongest available evidence: issue #34368 ('Rewind offers to undo file deletions it cannot actually restore') is a DIRECT, on-point confirmation that the native /rewind cannot recover Bash-deleted files — the exact gap A1 fills.
defects.fix: Add issue #34368 alongside #14002 as primary evidence for A1. It is a stronger citation than the 0-file race because it speaks precisely to deletions (A1's dominant irreversible class) and to /rewind advertising a restore it cannot deliver — reinforcing 'never advertise fully reversible'.

defects.issue: The 600ms/53ms/8.3%-overhead and FPR/FNR figures are imported from external papers (OAP, EviBound, the Claude Code auto-mode stress test) and treated as budget inputs, but the dossier's own gaps section concedes the actual checks the tribunal needs (URL resolution at scale, NLI entailment, independence clustering) are unmeasured and the ~8ms numbers are for cheap policy checks only. There is a latent risk the synchronous PreToolUse path (which blocks the tool for up to 600s) gets loaded with expensive network/NLI work and stalls the agent.
defects.fix: Explicitly split: cheap deterministic checks (hash/span/URL-resolve) run synchronously in the PreToolUse path; expensive checks (NLI/HHEM/MinHash clustering) run async (async hooks are supported) or post-hoc in the orchestrator, never inside the blocking 600s window. The dossier gestures at this in designImplications but should make it a hard constraint tied to the hook timeout primitive.

bullshitFlags: 'Build A0 as a synchronous PreToolUse/Bash hook' is correct for Bash, but the dossier silently generalizes it to 'every shippable assertion / file write / done message' WITHOUT acknowledging that the final 'done' message exits via no tool call and thus no PreToolUse hook — an unstated wrong assumption about which primitive fires when.

The 'tribunal' framing borrows the authority of EviBound's 100%->0% hallucination result, but that result is n=8 on code-execution artifacts with run_id + FINISHED markers — a fundamentally different, machine-checkable artifact than free-text research provenance. Presenting it as near-transferable to a self-critiquing multi-subagent loop is overclaiming the evidence; the dossier's gaps section admits this but the designImplications still lean on the 0% figure rhetorically.

Cross-platform A1 ('be cross-platform, user runs Windows') is asserted but the entire destructive-shape catalogue (rm, sed -i, find -delete, dd, git reset --hard) and the reflink/hardlink COW mechanism are POSIX-specific. Claiming cross-platform coverage while listing only Unix shapes and Unix copy primitives is hand-waving over the harder half of the problem (PowerShell command parsing + Windows snapshot mechanics).

The ~8.3% overhead figure is flagged in the dossier's own gaps as 'attached to two different mechanisms across papers — treat as soft', yet it reappears in three designImplications as a concrete budget target ('keep overhead near ~8%') without the soft-caveat. Reusing a number you've privately marked unreliable as a planning constant is mild overclaiming.

verdicts.verdict: Technically rigorous and code-verified, but it conflates two unrelated products and is overwhelmingly literature-driven rather than user-pain-driven. The findings that trace to actually-reported user defects (A4 fake "Jun26" freshness dates, A5 report blanking to skeleton) are excellent and ship-worthy. The rest (A0 provenance "tribunal" gate, A1 delete-snapshot hook, A2 trade-halt indicator) read as a solution-in-search-of-a-problem: no cited user ever reported them, they target a generic "Claude Code agent safety" product that is not CONQUER, and adoption friction is severe (fail-closed gates breed "verification theater" — the findings themselves concede this). Proceed, but only after splitting the work by whether a real user actually felt the pain.
strengths: A5 and A4(freshness) are anchored in ACTUAL logged user-visible defects (conquer_recording_defects.md: blank/jump 'f', 'Jun26 dates' h, '0-verified' g, stale price-stack c). These are the only findings where a real person experienced real pain — and they are correctly root-caused to render-state seams and last_verified=today stamping, not hand-waved. This is exactly the bar product work should clear.

Code claims were independently verifiable and held up: demote() codomain really is {single,inferred} (engine-light.ts:288-292), cleanCitations really does slice(0,4) with no domain dedupe (303-309), and runResearchBackbone really uses two bare Promise.all with no shared AbortController (306,325). Findings did not fabricate the evidence — rare and credit-worthy.

The A4 'count != independence' and 'last_verified=today is fake freshness' insights are genuinely user-protective: a user trusting a report because it shows '3 sources' when it's one syndicated wire, or '✓ verified today' when the source is 18 months old, is being actively misled. Fixing this is high-value and low-friction (build-time lint, distinct-domain count, no model in loop).

A4's 'keep ✓ unreachable at runtime and SAY SO via a legend' is a sharp product-honesty move — it reframes a limitation (engine can't emit ✓) as visible rigor instead of letting the user wonder why nothing is ever fully verified.

A3's user-facing framing is legitimate: an abandoned report silently burning 7x28s of paid Perplexity/Firecrawl spend is a real cost-to-user problem, correctly scoped as Priority-4 (cost/robustness, not outage).
mustFix: Separate the two products before proceeding. A0 (provenance gate), A1 (delete-snapshot Bash hook), and A2 (trade-halt indicator) are about a generic Claude-Code agent-safety / trading tool — NOT the CONQUER market-compass report product that A3/A4/A5 fix. Bundling them implies one roadmap. Decide explicitly which product this phase serves; do not let agent-safety research masquerade as CONQUER user-pain work.

Produce the user-pain ledger for EVERY A-item that lacks one. A4 and A5 cite conquer_recording_defects.md (real reported defects) — good. A0/A1/A2 cite only arXiv papers and vendor docs. Before building, name the actual user, the actual report, and the actual frequency for each. If no user ever hit it, it is a hypothesis, not a defect — gate it behind 'observed in the wild' first.

Resolve the fail-closed adoption-friction contradiction. The A0 findings simultaneously argue fail-closed→0% fabrication AND concede production fail-closed gates breed 'verification theater' (devs inspect output LESS after repeated false alarms — FPR 0.4-1.2%, FNR up to 81%). For a single-user, hands-off tool that already chose fail-open (demote+log), a blocking gate is net-negative for adoption. Justify per claim_class with the real over-block cost to THIS user, or keep fail-open.

defects.issue: A0/A1/A2 are framed as if they solve CONQUER user problems, but the 'problem' for each is sourced entirely from academic papers and vendor docs (arXiv 2603.20953, EviBound, Nasdaq RSS docs, Claude Code checkpointing docs) — no cited user ever reported a delete-disaster, a fabricated-provenance-shipped incident, or wanted a trade-halt flag. This is the classic solution-in-search-of-a-problem pattern.
defects.fix: For each, attach a real trigger: a logged incident, a user complaint, or a concrete near-miss. If none exists, demote from 'finding' to 'speculative backlog' and do not let it block the phase.

defects.issue: The A0 'tribunal' use case is admitted in the gaps section to have ZERO published evaluation — every cited benchmark gates code-execution artifacts (EviBound, n=8) or tool authorization (OAP), never free-text research claims. The 0%-fabrication and ~8% overhead numbers are borrowed from unrelated domains and tiny n, yet the design implications present them as load-bearing.
defects.fix: Stop quoting the 0%/8.3% figures as if they transfer. Run a small pilot on the tribunal's OWN corpus and report measured block-rate + FPR before locking thresholds. Label the cross-domain numbers as 'directional, unvalidated here.'

defects.issue: A2 (trade-halt indicator) has no user-need evidence at all and the gaps section admits it's unknown whether the tool even needs intraday halt state vs an at-open snapshot — i.e. the team isn't sure the feature is needed before designing freshness SLAs for it. Plus the deliverable is structurally capped at 60s-stale on free feeds, which the findings concede can miss the entire actionable LULD window (15s->pause).
defects.fix: Kill or park A2 until someone confirms a user wants a 'is this name paused?' flag AND that a 60s-stale flag is useful given the mechanism moves 4x faster. A feature that is admittedly too slow to be actionable is friction, not value.

defects.issue: A1 advertises a delete-snapshot safety net but the findings themselves note script-wrapped commands bypass PreToolUse interception and path resolution for globs/recursion is 'genuinely unsolved.' Shipping a 'safety net' with a known silent bypass class is worse for users than no net — it manufactures false confidence (the exact failure mode A4 warns about elsewhere).
defects.fix: If built, NEVER advertise reversibility; surface explicit 'NOT captured' classes to the user (mirroring Anthropic's own checkpointing warning). Fail closed (ask/deny) on any command shape it cannot snapshot, and say so in the UI. Otherwise the feature lies to the user.

defects.issue: A5 is correctly NOT marked DONE, but the two residual seams (cold-realm iframe reload, scroll-restoration jump) are explicitly 'unverified by any shipped fix note and uncovered by the 5-gate' — severity is inferred, not observed. The user impact (does a hard reload show a fast skeleton or a multi-minute progress screen?) is unknown.
defects.fix: Before sizing A5 remaining work, OBSERVE the actual behavior: hard-reload a settled report in the partitioned preview iframe and record what the user sees. Don't design fixes for a seam whose user-facing severity hasn't been witnessed.

defects.issue: The whole package optimizes provenance/honesty machinery but never asks whether the END USER (a single hands-off operator generating market-entry reports) actually reads or trusts confidence flags. If users skim the verdict and ignore ✓/⚠/? entirely, the elaborate gradeConfidence pipeline is invisible internal rigor, not adoption-driving value.
defects.fix: Add one user-facing validation: does the confidence grammar change a reader's trust or decision? If the legend/tooltips aren't noticed, prioritize the verdict-line honesty (A4 'verified today' on stale sources) over the deeper gate plumbing.

bullshitFlags: Cross-domain number laundering: '0% fabrication' (EviBound, n=8, code artifacts) and '~8.3% overhead' are repeatedly invoked to justify the A0 research-claim tribunal gate, while the gaps section quietly admits no published eval tests this use case and the overhead figure 'appears attached to two different mechanisms across papers — treat as soft.' The design implications do not carry that caveat forward.

'36.8% bypass / 81% end-to-end FNR' from arXiv 2604.04978 is cited as if it directly characterizes CONQUER's gate coverage. It characterizes Claude Code auto-mode in a stress test — a different system. Using it to assert CONQUER's ship paths will be routed around is an unproven transfer, even if the underlying caution (enumerate all ship paths) is reasonable.

Implicit claim that A0/A1/A2 belong to the same product/roadmap as A3/A4/A5. They do not — A1 is a Claude-Code Bash hook, A2 is a trading tool, while A3/A4/A5 are CONQUER report internals. The 'designImplications' list presents them as one coherent build with no acknowledgment that three of six items target a different product entirely.

'YoloFS as north-star v2' and the COW-filesystem framing dress up A1 as a mature roadmap when the findings concede reflink/hardlink per-delete latency is unmeasured and the only quantified overhead is from a different mechanism. Calling something a 'north-star' before measuring v1 feasibility is roadmap theater.

A2's '60-second delayed' is repeatedly stated as the achievable freshness, but the gaps section concedes that figure is a STATED tier delay with 'no measured distribution of real end-to-end halt-to-feed lag.' The freshness SLA is being designed around an unverified vendor claim.

verdicts.verdict: This spec survives the prosecution far better than most. I went hunting for fabricated citations, fake code references, and wrong Claude Code assumptions — the four things that usually sink a doc like this — and the load-bearing claims hold. Both arXiv IDs (2604.03173 hallucinated-URLs n>220k; 2604.04978 the 81% Claude-Code-auto-mode false-negative) are REAL papers with matching figures; ironically 2604.04978's actual finding (36.8% of dangerous actions bypass via file edits, not shell) is even stronger support for the coverage argument than the spec uses. The cited code at engine-light.ts:288 (demote) and :303 (cleanCitations) is verbatim accurate. The Claude Code primitives — decision:block on Stop, permissionDecision:'ask' on PreToolUse, stop_hook_active as the documented loop-guard, PreToolUse never seeing final prose — are all real and correctly mapped. This is the rare spec that earns its confidence on the verifiable layer. What it does NOT earn is the rhetorical layer: the prose is relentlessly self-congratulatory, several capability claims outrun what the code can mechanically do, and the honestLimitations section — though unusually good — is used as a shield that lets overclaims stand in the body. It is a strong PASS-with-conditions, not a clean checkmark. By its own grammar this verdict is a warn, not a checkmark — fitting.
strengths: Citations are real and accurately quoted. Both arXiv papers exist and the specific figures (3-13% hallucinated / 5-18% non-resolving, n>220k; 81% single-gate false-negative) match the sources. The spec even UNDER-uses 2604.04978: that paper's 36.8%-bypass-via-file-edits finding is a direct empirical anchor for the 'gate prose AND file/commit exits' design, yet the spec only cites the headline 81%.

Code references are precise, not vibes. engine-light.ts:288 (demote) and :303 (cleanCitations) exist exactly as described, and the generalization claim (recompute confidence server-side, force uncited→inferred regardless of model output) is faithful to what the code does — demote() literally returns 'inferred' when citeCount===0.

Claude Code primitives are correctly mapped — the usual failure mode for this kind of spec is absent. stop_hook_active (the loop guard), decision:block on Stop/SubagentStop, permissionDecision:'ask' on PreToolUse, and the structural insight that the final 'done' message is prose and thus invisible to PreToolUse are all real and correctly used as the load-bearing architecture.

The honestLimitations section is genuinely adversarial against itself — it concedes entailment is non-deterministic, that a pass is not a correctness guarantee, that coverage is an arms race citing the 81% bypass against its own gate, that the false-done detector false-positives on pure-analysis turns, and that the critic IS a Claude call with real latency/cost. This is the opposite of the overclaiming I default to expecting.

The safety model is structurally sound and not hand-waved: three INDEPENDENT bounds (ledger counter, stop_hook_active, critic maxTurns) with fail-open default and bound-checked-before-any-model-work directly answer the user's $100/2-day burn and no-Claude-at-runtime rule. The deterministic-kernel/model-at-edges split means the trusted verdict genuinely involves no LLM.
mustFix: Resolve the eat-your-own-dog-food contradiction in the verdict grammar. The spec says the kernel emits rung 'verified|single|inferred' AND that 'the checkmark is structurally reserved for human review' (mirroring engine-light's law that AI claims can never be ✓). A purely-deterministic kernel running with no human in the loop can therefore NEVER legitimately emit 'verified'. Either the 'verified' rung is dead/unreachable in the default path (then say so and remove it from the kernel output enum), or the checkmark-reserved-for-humans claim is violated. Pick one; right now the spec asserts both.

Downgrade or substantiate the 'verdict in seconds' / 'magic trick' first-run claim. The deterministic path that runs in seconds does NOT resolve URLs without network, yet the FABRICATED-CITATION detector (detector a) REQUIRES resolving every URL (curl -sI --max-time 5, up to SMELL_MAX_URLS=20). 20 URLs x up to 5s = up to 100s worst case, and the headline demo explicitly seeds a hallucinated arXiv URL whose detection DEPENDS on a network round-trip. The 'no model call, no network in the default deterministic path' claim and the 'resolve every cited URL' detector are in direct tension. State which detectors are network-free vs network-bound, and stop implying the citation check is instant.

Stop conflating the bound math. The spec claims 'worst-case cost bounded by per-turn cost x (1 + maxRevisions), zero Task() calls' — but the armed Stop path explicitly 'invokes the read-only critic for the prose indictment,' which is a subagent (Task-spawned, the spec itself says it 'returns only a text summary and shares no transcript'). So either the critic is a Task() call (then 'zero Task() calls' is false) or it is invoked some other way that must be named. Reconcile: the cost is per-turn-cost x (1+maxRevisions) PLUS up to (1+maxRevisions) Haiku critic invocations PLUS up to 20 URL fetches each. The honestLimitations section admits the critic cost; the coreLoop section denies it. Fix the coreLoop claim.

defects.issue: Self-contradiction between coreLoop ('zero Task() calls, zero new subagent fan-out' in the blocking path) and architecture/safetyModel (the Stop hook 'invokes the read-only critic', which is a subagent that 'returns only a text summary and shares no transcript' — the textbook description of a Task-spawned subagent). Both cannot be true.
defects.fix: State plainly: armed mode spawns exactly ONE bounded Haiku critic per revision (not zero), capped at maxTurns:6, and that is the ONLY model fan-out. Reserve 'zero subagent fan-out' for the UNARMED/deterministic-/smell path only, and label it as such.

defects.issue: The 'no network in the default deterministic path' claim is contradicted by detector (a) FABRICATED-CITATION, which requires resolving every URL, and by hooks/lib/checks.sh resolve_urls() via curl. URL resolution IS network. The spec wants both 'instant, network-free default' and 'we resolve every citation' — these are mutually exclusive for any output containing a URL.
defects.fix: Split the detectors explicitly into network-free (false-done, scope-drift, naked-confidence, lexeme/diff checks) and network-bound (citation resolution, span/hash match). Make citation-resolution a SEPARATE, clearly-flagged tier (like entailment) with its own timeout budget, and only call the network-free tier 'instant'. Update README's '60-second / verdict in seconds' demo to reflect that the seeded hallucinated-URL case incurs a network round-trip.

defects.issue: 'tests pass' after the test files were just edited → done.tests_gamed is presented as a deterministic detector, but detecting that an edit to a test file MADE the test pass (vs a legitimate test fix) is not mechanically decidable from a git diff alone. A developer fixing a genuinely-broken test then reporting 'tests pass' is indistinguishable from gaming by the proxy described. This is a hidden entailment-class judgment smuggled into the deterministic kernel.
defects.fix: Demote done.tests_gamed to a WARN-only heuristic (test files touched in same turn as a 'tests pass' claim → advise re-run from clean), never a BLOCK class. Move it out of failClosedClasses. The spec already lists done_contradicted as fail-closed; tests_gamed should NOT inherit that without a non-proxy signal (e.g. re-running the suite, which the read-only kernel cannot do).

defects.issue: Overclaim in differentiation: 'almost no agent-critique tool does correctly at once' and 'the credibility-defining property' — these are unfalsifiable marketing assertions with no competitive survey behind them. The spec provides zero evidence about what existing tools do; it asserts they are all 'are you sure? theater.' That is an unsupported blanket claim about a field the author has not enumerated.
defects.fix: Either cite 2-3 actual comparable tools (CodeRabbit, claude-code-hooks-mastery stop-hook enforcers, etc.) and say specifically what they lack, or soften to 'unlike naive same-model re-prompting' and drop the 'almost no tool does this' superlative.

defects.issue: The spec claims the critic 'sees ONLY the returned artifact + the kernel's deterministic findings (honoring no-shared-transcript)' as a SECURITY/independence property — but a Stop hook has transcript_path on stdin and the hook author controls exactly what is passed to the critic. 'No shared transcript' is a property of how Task subagents work by default, not a guarantee the design enforces; nothing stops the implementer from feeding the transcript in. It is presented as an architectural invariant when it is a convention.
defects.fix: Reword to 'we deliberately pass the critic only the returned artifact + kernel findings' (a design choice) rather than implying the runtime structurally prevents transcript sharing. Be honest that this is an enforced-by-our-own-code boundary, not a platform guarantee.

defects.issue: 'all primitives confirmed against code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, 2026-06-20' — the dated-confirmation stamp is exactly the kind of 'last_verified=today' freshness signal the kernel's recency() detector is built to KILL (config.json: 'recency() ... kills last_verified=today'). The spec stamps itself with the precise pattern it flags as gaming.
defects.fix: Drop the self-applied date stamp or replace with a checkable artifact (e.g. a committed docs snapshot hash). Do not assert today's-date verification in a doc whose own product treats today's-date verification as a red flag.

defects.issue: distinctDomains as the independence signal is described in the kernel detector list with confident framing ('distinct-DOMAIN dedupe ... drives the rung') while the honestLimitations correctly concedes it does NOT catch cross-domain syndication of a single wire story. The body text reads as a stronger independence guarantee than the limitation admits.
defects.fix: In the detector description itself (not only in honestLimitations), label it 'crude echo-gaming guard, not true source independence.' Keep the strong and the honest framing in the SAME place so a body-only reader is not misled.

bullshitFlags: OVERCLAIM: 'zero Task() calls, zero new subagent fan-out' in the blocking path — contradicted by the spec's own statement that the Stop hook invokes the read-only critic subagent. The armed path spawns one critic per revision.
OVERCLAIM/CONTRADICTION: 'no network in the default deterministic path' vs the FABRICATED-CITATION detector that resolves every URL via curl. URL resolution is network; it cannot be both.

HAND-WAVING: done.tests_gamed presented as a deterministic BLOCK-class detector when distinguishing a legitimate test fix from test-gaming is an entailment-class judgment not decidable from a git diff. A fuzzy check is smuggled into the 'model-free' kernel.
UNSUPPORTED BLANKET CLAIM: 'almost no agent-critique tool does this correctly at once' / existing tools are all 'are you sure? theater' — asserted with zero competitive evidence or enumeration.
OVERSTATED INVARIANT: 'honoring no-shared-transcript' framed as an architectural guarantee, when it is a convention the hook author can trivially violate by passing transcript_path to the critic.
SELF-INCRIMINATING FRESHNESS STAMP: 'confirmed ... 2026-06-20' is the exact last_verified=today pattern config.json says recency() should kill — the spec games the signal its own product flags.

MILD: 'magic trick, not a setup chore' / 'verdict in seconds' first-run framing oversells latency for any output containing URLs, where the citation check incurs up to ~100s of fetches in the worst case.

verdicts.verdict: A genuinely strong design that is more honest and better-mapped to Claude Code than 95% of "self-critique" tooling — but it leans its entire runaway-loop safety story on a primitive (stop_hook_active) that I could NOT find in the very doc it cites (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, fetched 2026-06-20). That doc redirects from the old anthropic.com URL and now describes a richer event model (MessageDisplay, defer permission, async/asyncRewake, prompt/http/mcp_tool hook types) that the spec ignores. Two of the three "independent" stops are actually correlated, the only documented backstop is a 600s timeout that is too slow to be a safety net for a user burned by uncapped loops, and the Stop-hook critic that invokes Haiku per turn is doing exactly the kind of model-in-the-loop work the doc implicitly warns against. The deterministic kernel, read-only critic, fail-open posture, and dogfooded confidence grammar are excellent and the CONQUER demote()/cleanCitations() lineage at engine-light.ts:288/:303 is real and accurately cited. But before this proceeds, every hook-mechanic claim must be re-verified against the CURRENT schema on the user's actual installed version, because the spec is written against a stale mental model of the API and parades that as "all primitives confirmed against the docs."
strengths: The core architectural insight is correct and load-bearing: a 'done' claim is prose, not a tool call, so PreToolUse can never gate it and Stop/SubagentStop is the only locus that can. The fetched docs confirm Stop/SubagentStop support decision:block + additionalContext and that 'the conversation continues so Claude can act on the feedback' — so the loop engine itself is real.

The deterministic-kernel-model-at-the-edges split is the right call and is faithfully derived from LIVE, verified code: demote() at market-compass/src/lib/conquer/engine-light.ts:288 and cleanCitations() at :303 do exactly what the spec claims (force any uncited claim to 'inferred' regardless of model output, dedupe citations). This is not an invented judge; it is a battle-tested pattern being generalized. That lineage is the spec's strongest credibility anchor.

Read-only critic subagent (tools: Read/Grep/Glob/WebFetch, no Write/Edit/Bash, maxTurns cap) is a sound mitigation for 'never let the LLM grade its own homework' — it physically cannot rubber-stamp by editing the artifact, and re-scoring its indictment deterministically is the right trust model.

Fail-OPEN-by-default with trap-guarded no-op on any internal error is the correct posture for a day-one gate and directly answers the over-block / verification-theater risk. Defaulting aggressive classes off and requiring a corpus pilot (eval/) before flipping anything to fail-closed is genuinely disciplined engineering.

The honestLimitations section is unusually candid and mostly accurate — it concedes entailment is non-deterministic, coverage is an arms race bounded by hooked exits, the false-done detector uses cheap proxies that false-positive on pure-analysis turns, no real independence clustering, and that the critic IS a Claude call with real latency/cost. This is the opposite of overclaiming and earns trust.

The eval/corpus + over-block measurement gate before locking thresholds is the single most important piece of engineering rigor in the whole spec — it means the thresholds are empirical, not asserted.

defects.issue: THE BLOCKER: stop_hook_active — named as one of the three independent runaway-loop stops and cited as 'the runtime's built-in stop_hook_active flag' — does NOT appear anywhere in code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks as fetched 2026-06-20 (I searched the full page twice; the doc explicitly has no re-entrancy flag, counter, or invocation-count field). The spec claims 'all primitives confirmed against code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, 2026-06-20'. Either the flag was removed/renamed in the current event model, or it was never in this doc and the spec is relying on folklore from the older Anthropic docs. If stop_hook_active does not exist on the user's installed version, stop #2 of the triple-bound silently evaporates and the loop's safety collapses to the ledger counter alone — for a user who burned $100 on uncapped loops, this is unacceptable.
defects.fix: Empirically confirm the field on the user's ACTUAL installed Claude Code build: add a Stop hook that dumps stdin to a file and inspect whether stop_hook_active (or any re-entrancy field) is present. If absent, DO NOT ship the triple-bound claim. Re-architect the re-entrancy guard to be self-owned: write the session_id + a monotonically incrementing iteration token to the ledger BEFORE returning block, and treat the ledger counter as the primary (not secondary) re-entrancy guard. Demote stop_hook_active to 'opportunistic if present'. Update the safetyModel prose to stop calling it 'the runtime's built-in flag'.

defects.issue: The three 'independent, redundant stops' are not independent. (a) stop_hook_active (unverified) and (b) the ledger block-count both gate the SAME Stop-hook entry point and both depend on the same JSONL read/parse succeeding — if jq fails or the ledger is corrupt/locked, fail-open is invoked, which means BOTH counter-based stops are bypassed simultaneously by a single failure. (c) The critic's maxTurns caps the CRITIC's internal turns, not the outer PRODUCE->REVISE loop — it does nothing to bound how many times the agent re-enters Stop. So the actual outer-loop bound is effectively ONE mechanism (the ledger counter) with a fail-open escape hatch, not three.
defects.fix: Make the bounds genuinely orthogonal: (1) ledger counter as primary; (2) an independent in-memory/session-flag check that does NOT share the ledger's failure mode; (3) a hard wall-clock or absolute-iteration ceiling enforced even on the fail-open path (i.e. fail-open must STILL allow the stop, never re-block, when any ambiguity exists — verify the code does this). Stop describing maxTurns as an outer-loop bound; it isn't one. Re-word safetyModel to claim the honest number of truly-independent stops (likely 2, with fail-open as the ultimate backstop).

defects.issue: The Stop critic invokes Haiku synchronously inside the hook on every armed turn, and the spec says jq validates its JSON and the kernel re-scores it before deciding. The fetched docs give Stop hooks a 600-second default timeout — so a slow/hung Haiku call does NOT get killed quickly; it can stall the turn for up to 10 minutes before fail-open triggers. For a latency- and cost-sensitive user, a per-turn synchronous model call gated only by a 10-minute timeout is a real UX and (mild) cost footgun, and it contradicts the spirit of 'no LLM in the blocking default path' since /smell-loop arming puts the critic squarely IN the blocking path.
defects.fix: Set an explicit, short per-hook timeout in settings.json for stop-critic (e.g. 20-30s) rather than inheriting 600s.
