Better: use the doc's documented async/asyncRewake mechanism for the critic so the kernel verdict (deterministic, fast) blocks and the critic runs out-of-band, injecting its indictment via additionalContext on a later rewake. Make the deterministic kernel the ONLY thing in the synchronous blocking window; the critic should never be able to stall a turn.

defects.issue: extract-evidence.mjs and checks.sh shell out to git (git diff --stat, git status) and curl inside hook windows, and the kernel is described as having 'no network in the blocking window' while checks.sh has resolve_urls() via curl. These are in tension. More concretely: the false-done detector's 'empty git diff under done claim' signal is unreliable — it false-positives on every legitimate pure-analysis/research/answer turn (correctly conceded in limitations) AND false-negatives whenever the repo isn't a git repo, the work happened outside the cwd, or the diff is staged/stashed. Running in a non-git directory (very common) makes git diff error, which the fail-open trap will swallow, silently disabling the headline detector with no signal to the user.
defects.fix: Detect non-git / git-error conditions explicitly and emit a 'notChecked: done.empty_diff (no git context)' entry rather than silently fail-opening — otherwise the ledger will show clean PASSes that actually checked nothing, which is the exact silent-unexplained-behavior (PP-10) the tool claims to cure. Gate the empty-diff signal on claimClass so it only fires for completion claims that assert file changes, never on analysis turns.

defects.issue: Cross-platform fragility: the perimeter hooks are .sh files (POSIX) but the user is on Windows 11 / PowerShell primary, and the spec itself notes guard-destructive.sh must be 'POSIX + PowerShell aware.' A .sh hook on Windows requires Git Bash to be on PATH and invoked correctly by the Claude Code hook runner; if the runner executes hooks via cmd/PowerShell, the .sh shebang won't resolve and the hook silently no-ops (fail-open) — disabling the destructive-command guard, the ONE fail-closed protection, on the user's own machine. The install.sh idempotent-merge-into-settings.json step has the same exposure.
defects.fix: Do not ship shell-script hooks as the primary on a PowerShell-primary box. Make the hook commands invoke node directly (node bin/guard-destructive.mjs) so the bundled node runs them identically on Windows/macOS/Linux, with all shell-specific regex logic inside the .mjs. Test the destructive guard end-to-end on Windows BEFORE claiming PP-07 coverage; a fail-open destructive guard is worse than none because it creates false confidence.

defects.issue: Spec ignores documented capabilities of the very doc it cites that would materially improve it: (a) MessageDisplay event ('while assistant message text is displayed') — the spec asserts 'no hook ever sees the final NL message' and that Stop is 'the ONLY locus,' but MessageDisplay sees message text (display-only, can't block, but relevant to the coverage claim). (b) 'defer' permissionDecision value exists alongside allow/deny/ask. (c) prompt/http/mcp_tool hook types and async/asyncRewake exist. Writing 'all primitives confirmed against the docs' while missing these signals the spec was validated against a stale snapshot.
defects.fix: Re-audit against the current event model. Soften 'the ONLY locus that sees the final message' to 'the only locus that sees it AND can block.' Decide explicitly whether 'defer' is useful for the destructive guard. Re-state the primitives-confirmed claim with the actual doc date AND the installed CLI version number, since the doc evolves.

defects.issue: The /smell command frontmatter declares allowed-tools: Bash(node *) and Read, but the kernel is invoked 'on the last message.' A slash command does not have structured access to the prior assistant message as a parameter — it would have to scrape the transcript_path or rely on the model pasting the last output into the kernel, which reintroduces the model into the trusted path (the model decides what text to grade). This undercuts the 'deterministic, model cannot author the verdict' guarantee for the manual /smell surface specifically.
defects.fix: For /smell, read the last assistant message from transcript_path deterministically (same parse path as the Stop hook's extract-evidence.mjs) rather than depending on the model to feed the kernel its own output. Share one extraction code path between the hook and the command so the manual surface has the same integrity guarantee as the automated one.

defects.issue: Maintenance burden / arms-race honesty gap: the false-done detector keys on a hardcoded English lexeme set ('complete','done','tests pass','implemented'). This is trivially evaded (paraphrase, non-English, markdown emphasis) and will rot. The spec markets PP-03 false-completion as 'the primary target' and 'the headline,' but a regex lexeme matcher is a weak mechanism for the headline claim — it catches the naive case the user has already learned to distrust, not the adversarial one.
defects.fix: Be explicit in README/honestLimitations that false-done detection is a lexeme heuristic, not semantic completion-checking, and will miss paraphrased completion lies (the limitations section gestures at this but the differentiation/targetPainPoints sections oversell it as the headline). Consider anchoring on the structural side-signal (claim-of-change + empty-diff) as primary and the lexeme as a secondary trigger, since the structural signal is harder to evade than vocabulary.

bullshitFlags: 'all primitives confirmed against code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, 2026-06-20' — OVERCLAIM. stop_hook_active, a named load-bearing primitive, does not appear in that doc as fetched on that exact date. The doc also contains events/values the spec doesn't mention (MessageDisplay, defer, async/asyncRewake, prompt/http/mcp_tool hook types), indicating the spec was validated against an older mental model and the confirmation claim is stronger than the evidence supports.

'three independent stops' / 'triple-bounded so it can never run away' — OVERCLAIM. Two of the three share the same Stop-hook entry point and the same ledger-read failure mode (so they fall together under one jq/IO failure), and the critic's maxTurns bounds the critic, not the outer revise loop. The honest count of truly-independent outer-loop bounds is closer to one-plus-fail-open. 'Can never run away' is an absolute claim a redundant-but-correlated design cannot earn.

'zero network in the blocking path' / 'no LLM in the blocking default path' — PARTIALLY MISLEADING. True only when /smell-loop is disarmed. Once armed (the entire point of the loop product), the Haiku critic and checks.sh curl URL-resolution run in the Stop window under a 600s timeout. The qualifier 'default' is doing very heavy lifting; a reader skims this as 'never blocks on a model call,' which is false in the armed configuration the spec spends most of its words describing.

'the first run must feel like a magic trick, not a setup chore' / 'instant value, zero config' — ASPIRATIONAL, not a technical claim. On a PowerShell-primary Windows box, an install.sh + .sh hooks path is precisely a setup chore (Git Bash dependency, PATH, settings.json merge), and a silently-failing-open hook on Windows produces a magic trick of the wrong kind (no protection, clean-looking PASSes). Adoption-lens framing is fine, but it's marketing copy sitting inside an architecture section.

'binds every exit that actually carries an overclaim' — OVERCLAIM, and the spec partially concedes this in limitations. It binds prose (Stop), Bash (PreToolUse), and Edit/Write (PostToolUse). Mid-stream output the user reads before Stop, MCP-tool exfil, and tool-combination writes are unhooked — 'every exit' contradicts the spec's own honest coverage caveat.

External benchmark numbers (3-13% hallucinated URLs, 81% single-gate bypass, n>221k) are cited with specific arXiv ids (2604.03173, 2604.04978) — I did NOT verify these papers exist or report these figures; given the 2026 dates and the spec's own concession that these are 'analogical priors,' treat the precise percentages as unverified motivating priors, not established facts about THIS tool's performance. The spec is mostly honest about this in limitations, but the problem/differentiation sections deploy the numbers with more authority than 'analogical prior' warrants.
mustFix: Empirically verify stop_hook_active (or whatever re-entrancy field exists) on the user's ACTUAL installed Claude Code build by dumping Stop-hook stdin to a file. If absent or renamed, re-architect the re-entrancy guard around a self-owned ledger iteration token and STOP claiming a runtime-provided flag. The runaway-loop safety story cannot ship on an unverified primitive for this specific user.

Re-audit ALL hook-mechanic claims against the CURRENT code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks schema (which now includes MessageDisplay, defer, async/asyncRewake, and prompt/http/mcp_tool hook types) and against the installed CLI version. Replace 'all primitives confirmed' with the verified version number, and correct the now-stale claims (the 'only locus that sees the final message' and the independence/triple-bound count).

Set an explicit short timeout (~20-30s) for the stop-critic hook instead of inheriting the 600s default, OR move the critic out of the synchronous blocking window via the documented async/asyncRewake path. A 10-minute potential stall on an armed Stop is unacceptable for a user sensitive to runaway/cost and contradicts the safety thesis.

Replace POSIX .sh hooks with node-invoked .mjs hooks (node bin/*.mjs) as the primary, and test the destructive-command guard (PP-07) AND the install/settings-merge end-to-end on the user's Windows 11 / PowerShell environment. A silently fail-open destructive guard on the user's own OS is a false-confidence hazard worse than no guard.

Prove the fail-open path can NEVER re-block: write and run the test/smell.test.mjs cases the spec promises (stop_hook_active/ledger>=max -> always allow; jq parse failure -> allow; corrupt ledger -> allow) on the real runtime before arming /smell-loop. The loop must be demonstrated bounded by execution, not asserted bounded by design.

Make 'silently checked nothing' impossible: when git context is absent, a URL can't resolve, or the critic crashes, the ledger must record an explicit notChecked entry rather than a clean PASS — otherwise the tool reproduces the silent-unexplained-behavior (PP-10) it claims to cure.

verdicts.verdict: The spec's strategic read of the platform is unusually good — it correctly identifies that the final 'done' message is prose (not a tool call) and that only Stop/SubagentStop sees it, that decision:block is the continuation engine, that stop_hook_active is the runtime's loop-breaker, that PreToolUse permissionDecision:'ask' is the right downgrade, and that a Task subagent returns only text with no shared transcript. Those are all correct and load-bearing. But the architecture rests on one mechanically-wrong assumption that recurs everywhere: a shell Stop hook cannot 'invoke the read-only critic subagent.' Subagents are spawned only by the orchestrating model via the Task tool; a hook is an external process that can at best shell out to a fresh headless `claude -p` (a new process with its own cost and loop), which is NOT the in-session .claude/agents/smell-critic.md subagent and does NOT inherit its tools/maxTurns frontmatter. This collapses the 'parallel critic in the Stop hook' design (architecture plane 2 & 4, coreLoop step 5) and undermines two of the three claimed bounds. Combined with a self-contradicting bound model (stop_hook_active is a single boolean that already caps continuations at ~1, making maxRevisions=2 unreachable via that path) and a likely-nonexistent subagent-frontmatter maxTurns field, the safety story is less airtight than asserted. The CONQUER citations check out structurally (demote at engine-light.ts:288, cleanCitations at :303 are real and exactly as cited) but the spec overstates them: gradeConfidence({distinctDomains,sourceAgeMonths,isProjection,humanReviewed}) does NOT exist — the real demote() is 4 lines taking (raw, citeCount) only — and cleanCitations does registrable-domain dedupe nowhere (that logic lives in brand-name derivation at :1484-1512). The design is salvageable but must resolve the hook-cannot-spawn-subagent problem and fix the bound arithmetic before proceeding.
strengths: Correctly nails the single most important and most-often-misunderstood Claude Code fact: the agent's natural-language 'done' is not a tool call, no PreToolUse hook ever sees it, and Stop/SubagentStop is the only locus that does. This is right and is the spec's best insight.

Correctly uses decision:block + reason on Stop as the revision-forcing mechanism, and correctly identifies the runtime's built-in stop_hook_active re-entrancy flag as the loop-breaker — these are real documented behaviors, not invented.

Correctly maps PreToolUse to a permissionDecision:'ask' downgrade (via hookSpecificOutput) rather than a hard deny, and correctly reads the stdin payload fields (session_id, transcript_path, stop_hook_active) that hooks actually receive.

Correctly honors the subagent contract: a Task-spawned subagent returns only a text summary and shares no transcript, so grading the returned artifact (not hidden reasoning) is the right and only available design.

The CONQUER anchors are real and accurately located: demote() at engine-light.ts:288 and cleanCitations() at :303 exist verbatim and do recompute confidence server-side independent of the model's self-report — a legitimate proof-of-pattern.
mustFix: Resolve the core mechanism error: a shell Stop hook CANNOT invoke the .claude/agents/smell-critic.md subagent — subagents are spawned only by the orchestrating model via the Task tool. Either (a) drop the critic from the blocking hook path and make it a model-invoked Task in the cooperative skill, or (b) have the hook shell out to an explicit headless `claude -p` call and rename/re-scope it honestly as a separate process (with its own cost + bound), NOT the in-session subagent. Every reference to 'the hook invokes/runs the critic subagent' (architecture 2 & 4, coreLoop step 5, safetyModel) must be corrected.

Fix the bound arithmetic. stop_hook_active is a single boolean, not a per-iteration counter; once the hook blocks and the model re-enters Stop, stop_hook_active==true forces an allow — which already caps forced revisions at ~1, making the ledger maxRevisions=2 path unreachable through that mechanism. State precisely which of the 'three independent stops' actually fires when, and reconcile maxRevisions=2 with the one-shot nature of stop_hook_active.

Drop or verify maxTurns as subagent-markdown frontmatter. Documented agent frontmatter is name/description/tools/model; maxTurns is a Task/SDK option, not agent.md frontmatter. As written it is presented as a 'third independent bound' that likely does not exist where claimed — and is unreachable anyway given the hook-can't-spawn-subagent problem.

Correct the CONQUER overclaims: gradeConfidence({distinctDomains,sourceAgeMonths,isProjection,humanReviewed}) is NOT in engine-light.ts and is NOT 'lifted directly from demote()' (demote is `(raw, citeCount) -> single|inferred`, 4 lines). cleanCitations does NOT dedupe by registrable domain (it filters a valid-id Set and slices to 4). Reword to 'inspired by / generalizing' and design the new logic as net-new rather than implying it already ships.

defects.issue: Architecture planes (2) and (4) and coreLoop step 5 assume a Stop hook can 'invoke the read-only critic subagent' and run it 'in parallel.' Hooks are external shell processes; they cannot call the Task tool or load .claude/agents/*. The subagent is reachable only by the orchestrating model.
defects.fix: Make the critic a model-invoked Task inside the self-critique skill (cooperative path), and keep the BLOCKING hook path purely deterministic Node (no critic). If an adversarial second model is wanted in the hook, spawn an explicit `claude -p` headless process, bound and labeled as such — and account for its cost in the safety model.

defects.issue: Self-contradicting loop bound: the spec treats stop_hook_active as equivalent to an N-count counter, but it is a one-shot boolean. After the first block, re-entry sets it true and the hook must allow, capping forced revisions at 1 — so SMELL_MAX_REVISIONS=2 is never reached via that path. The 'three independent stops' are not independent.
defects.fix: Either accept a 1-revision cap honestly, or implement the multi-revision loop entirely via the ledger counter and explicitly handle stop_hook_active (e.g. only honor stop_hook_active as the final hard backstop, and gate continuations on ledger count < max while stop_hook_active is false). Spell out the exact state machine.

defects.issue: maxTurns:6 is claimed as subagent frontmatter and as one of the three safety bounds. It is not a documented agent.md frontmatter field (it's a Task/SDK option), and the subagent isn't even reachable from the hook, so this bound is doubly unfounded.
defects.fix: Remove maxTurns from agent frontmatter claims; if a turn cap is needed, enforce it via the Task call options in the model-invoked path, and re-derive the safety bound count accordingly (likely two real stops, not three).

defects.issue: safetyModel claim 'NO network / NO LLM ... IN THE BLOCKING DEFAULT PATH' conflicts with coreLoop step 5 running the critic (an LLM call) and re-scoring its indictment before the DECIDE step, plus checks.sh resolve_urls() via curl in the gate. If the critic and URL resolution run synchronously in the Stop window, the blocking path DOES include network+LLM.
defects.fix: Make the default armed path deterministic-only (kernel + cheap git side-signals, no curl, no critic) and move URL resolution + critic to an explicit async/advisory tier that never gates. Reword the safety claim to match. honestLimitations #8 already concedes the critic adds latency — align the architecture text with that concession.

defects.issue: 'disable-model-invocation' frontmatter is relied on for /smell and /smell-loop. Slash commands are user-typed surfaces; the exact key and its semantics should be verified against current docs rather than asserted. Risk of a non-existent/renamed field.
defects.fix: Verify the precise frontmatter key for preventing model auto-invocation of a command (vs. it simply being user-invoked by nature). If unsupported, rely on the fact that commands are user-invoked and drop the claim, or move the guarantee to the skill's description gating.

defects.issue: PostToolUse/Edit|Write 'note-blind-edit' depends on an 'in-session read-set' to know which files were Read. Hooks are stateless processes; there is no built-in per-session read-set exposed to a PostToolUse hook. Reconstructing it requires parsing transcript_path, which the spec never specifies for this hook.
defects.fix: Specify that note-blind-edit parses transcript_path to build the read-set, or maintain the read-set in the ledger/.smelltest state updated by a PreToolUse(Read) hook. Acknowledge the cost/fragility of transcript parsing.

defects.issue: The spec implies SubagentStop will catch the critic's own completion in the loop, but SubagentStop fires for ANY subagent the main agent spawns — wiring stop-critic.sh to both Stop and SubagentStop risks the gate firing on unrelated subagents (and potentially on its own critic if that path existed), creating spurious blocks or recursion.
defects.fix: Scope the SubagentStop handler to no-op for the smell-critic and for subagents whose output isn't a user-facing 'done' claim; document which subagent completions are in-scope.

bullshitFlags: 'invokes the read-only critic subagent' from within a Stop/PreToolUse hook — hooks cannot spawn or call subagents; this is the spec's central platform-mechanism error, repeated across architecture, coreLoop, and safetyModel.

'three independent stops' / 'triple-bounded' — overstated: stop_hook_active is a one-shot boolean (caps at ~1 revision, not N), maxTurns is not valid agent frontmatter and is unreachable from the hook, leaving effectively one real deterministic bound (the ledger). The redundancy is marketed, not mechanical.

'gradeConfidence({distinctDomains,sourceAgeMonths,isProjection,humanReviewed}) lifted directly from CONQUER demote() at engine-light.ts:288' — fabricated specificity; the real demote() takes (raw, citeCount) and is 4 lines with none of those parameters. It is an aspiration dressed as existing, battle-tested code.

'distinct-DOMAIN dedupe (not raw id) per :303, generalizing the cleanCitations domain gap' — cleanCitations at :303 does no domain logic at all (it filters a valid-id Set and slices to 4); registrable-domain handling lives elsewhere (:1484-1512) for brand naming. The cited line does not support the claim.

'NO network / NO LLM in the blocking default path' asserted in safetyModel while coreLoop step 5 runs the critic LLM and re-scores it before DECIDE, and checks.sh curls URLs — the blocking-path-is-pure claim contradicts the described flow.

'all primitives confirmed against code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, 2026-06-20' — presented as verification, but the hook-spawns-subagent and maxTurns-frontmatter claims are exactly the kind of thing that doc would contradict; the confirmation stamp is asserted, not demonstrated.

verdicts.verdict: smelltest targets a real, frequent, trust-breaking problem (false "done", fabricated citations, scope drift) that is squarely in this user's lived pain — verified against the CONQUER codebase, the $100-burn memory, and the no-Claude-at-runtime rule. The safety model is the strongest part: triple-bounded, fail-open, off-by-default, ask-not-deny. But the product story has a structural gap the spec papers over: the headline ("refuses to accept done until it survives a prosecutor") is OFF by default, because the only way to get auto-blocking is to arm /smell-loop, which taxes EVERY turn with a Haiku call plus up to 20 URL fetches — and the default WARN mode blocks nothing except destructive commands. So the tagline describes the armed/aggressive config, while the install gives you an advisory annotator. That is a "solution that demos as a magic trick but lives as a novelty" risk: most users run /smell once, never arm the loop, and the corrosive false-done class keeps escaping. Combined with a false-done detector whose cheapest proxy (empty-diff-under-done) will false-positive on every pure-analysis/Q&A turn, adoption friction is higher than the "trivial install, instant value" framing claims. Not blocking-grade flaws — the design is mostly honest about these in honestLimitations — but the gap between the promised experience and the default experience must be closed before this proceeds.
strengths: Solves a REAL, repeatedly-logged, trust-breaking problem, not an invented one. False completion, fabricated citations, and scope drift are the most corrosive Claude Code behaviors and are consistent with this user's own history (the verified $100/2-day burn memory, the no-Claude-at-runtime rule). This is the opposite of a solution in search of a problem.

The enforcement-locus insight is correct and non-obvious: the final 'done' message is prose, not a tool call, so no PreToolUse hook ever sees it — gating it at Stop/SubagentStop is the right call and is what most 'are you sure?' critics get wrong. This is a genuine product differentiator, not vendor-doc vibes.

Safety posture is the standout: triple-bound (ledger counter + stop_hook_active + critic maxTurns), fail-open on any error, off-until-armed, network/LLM-free in the blocking default path, and ask-not-deny on destructive commands. This is precisely engineered against THIS user's scar tissue and earns trust.

The deterministic-kernel-over-model-confidence principle is real and verifiable — it generalizes CONQUER's live demote()/cleanCitations() (confirmed at engine-light.ts:288 and :303), which already recompute confidence server-side and force uncited claims to 'inferred'. Grounding the design in a battle-tested function the user already trusts is strong adoption psychology.

It eats its own dog food (every verdict carries the confidence grammar; checkmark reserved for human review) and ships an append-only ledger so a block is explainable claim-by-claim — directly answers the silent-unexplained-behavior pain (PP-10) and pre-empts the 'why did it block me' frustration that kills gating tools.

defects.issue: Tagline/headline describes the ARMED config, but the default install is advisory-only. 'Refuses to accept done until it survives a prosecutor' is the promise; yet mode:'warn' is the default, and in WARN mode nothing blocks except the irreversible-data-loss class. The auto-critic that actually catches false-done requires manually arming /smell-loop. A user who installs and reads the tagline will expect blocking out of the box and get annotations. This is the exact overclaim-vs-default-behavior gap the tool exists to catch.
defects.fix: Rewrite the tagline and README quickstart to state plainly: 'default = advisory annotator; arm /smell-loop for enforcement.' Make the 60-second demo show BOTH the default WARN annotation AND an explicit 'now run /smell-loop to make it block' step, so the promised experience and the default experience are the same thing the user actually sees.

defects.issue: The armed loop taxes EVERY turn. Each armed Stop adds a Haiku critic call + up to SMELL_MAX_URLS (20) network round-trips, on every single turn of the core dev loop — not just suspicious ones. For a user this cost-sensitive, that is a per-turn latency and (small but nonzero) cost tax that will get the loop disarmed within a day, leaving the tool as a manual /smell novelty.
defects.fix: Gate the expensive paths behind a cheap pre-filter: only invoke the critic / fire URL resolution when the deterministic kernel already found a citation, a completion lexeme, or a scope-drift signal. A turn with no citations and no 'done' claim should cost ZERO network and ZERO model — short-circuit to silent-allow. Make this short-circuit the documented default so 'armed' is cheap on the 90% of turns that carry no overclaim.

defects.issue: The cheapest false-done proxy (empty git diff under a 'done' lexeme) will false-positive on the most common turn type: pure analysis, Q&A, research, planning, and 'I read X, here is my answer' turns produce no diff and frequently contain words like 'complete'/'done'/'implemented'. In WARN mode this is noise; if a user ever flips done-contradicted to fail-closed (the spec invites this), it becomes a workflow-bricking false block on legitimate answers.
defects.fix: Require a co-occurring concrete completion CLAIM about code/files (e.g. 'tests pass', 'implemented the function', 'committed') AND a code-bearing intent signal before empty-diff can fire — never on a bare 'done'/'complete' lexeme in an analytical answer. Add explicit clean-control analysis turns to eval/corpus/ and report the false-positive rate on them before any fail-closed flip is permitted.

defects.issue: Adoption claim 'zero config, no API keys, no model call in the default path' quietly conflicts with the value proposition. The default deterministic path that needs no model is ALSO the path that catches the least (citations + scope + destructive). The thing users came for — catching false 'done' adversarially — is the part that DOES cost a model call and ISN'T on by default. The 'magic trick first run' (/smell) only re-grades the last output deterministically; it does not demonstrate the prosecutor at all.
defects.fix: Make the first-run /smell demo seed a case that the DETERMINISTIC kernel alone catches with a visible BLOCK (hallucinated arXiv URL + TODO-only 'Implementation complete!'), so the magic-trick moment uses the free path and is genuinely impressive without the critic. Reserve the critic as the clearly-labeled 'arm this for the adversarial layer' upsell.

defects.issue: Citation-precision overclaim in the spec itself: it states distinct-domain dedupe 'generalizes the cleanCitations domain gap noted at engine-light.ts:303.' Verified — cleanCitations at :303 has NO domain logic and NO 'noted gap'; it is a string-membership filter with slice(0,4). Registrable-domain logic exists elsewhere (domainOf at :4000, R34 root logic at :1484+) but not where cited. This is decorative line-number precision attached to a function that doesn't do the implied thing — ironically the failure mode smelltest claims to detect.
defects.fix: Correct the reference to cite the function that actually does registrable-domain extraction (domainOf / the R34 root logic), or state honestly that domain-dedupe is NEW code inspired by the cleanCitations pattern. Do not imply an existing 'gap was noted' that isn't in the code.

defects.issue: Problem-validation provenance is unverifiable from the workspace. The '775 de-duped pain observations' and the PP-## taxonomy are the load-bearing evidence that this is a real/frequent problem, but no corpus artifact exists in the repo, and the two arXiv IDs (2604.03173, 2604.04978) are future-dated and not checkable. The spec partly concedes the arXiv numbers are 'analogical priors,' but the 775-observation taxonomy is presented as established fact.
defects.fix: Ship the pain-observation corpus (or a redacted sample + methodology) as eval/corpus/provenance so the PP-## codes are auditable, and label the arXiv figures as unverified motivating priors everywhere they appear, not just in honestLimitations.

bullshitFlags: Tagline 'refuses to accept done until it survives a prosecutor' overclaims the default: enforcement (blocking + the critic) is OFF until /smell-loop is armed; the default install is an advisory annotator that blocks nothing but destructive commands.

'Trivial install, instant value, zero config — the first run must feel like a magic trick' overstates the out-of-box payoff: /smell only re-grades the last message deterministically and never invokes the adversarial prosecutor that the whole pitch is built around.

'Generalizes the cleanCitations domain gap noted at engine-light.ts:303' — verified false: cleanCitations at :303 contains no domain logic and notes no gap (it is a membership filter + slice(0,4)). Precise-line-number citation dressed onto a function that doesn't do the implied thing.

'No model call in the default deterministic path' is technically true but rhetorically misleading — it omits that the headline capability (adversarial false-done catching) is exactly the part that requires a model call and is therefore not in the default path.

'775 de-duped pain observations' and the PP-## taxonomy are presented as established fact but are not locatable as an artifact in the workspace and cannot be verified; the arXiv IDs are future-dated and unverifiable.
mustFix: Close the promise-vs-default gap: rewrite the tagline/README so the install's DEFAULT behavior (advisory WARN, enforcement off) is what the user is promised, with arming /smell-loop presented as the explicit step to get blocking — no implying out-of-box prosecution.

Add a cheap pre-filter so the armed loop costs ZERO model + ZERO network on turns with no citation, no completion lexeme, and no scope signal — otherwise the per-turn Haiku+20-fetch tax gets the loop disarmed and the core value never lands.

Harden the false-done detector against analysis/Q&A false positives: never fire empty-diff-under-done on a bare completion lexeme; require a co-occurring concrete code-completion claim. Prove the false-positive rate on clean analytical-turn controls in eval/corpus/ BEFORE any class is allowed to flip fail-closed.

Correct the engine-light.ts:303 'domain gap' citation to reference the function that actually does registrable-domain logic (or label the dedupe as new code), so the spec doesn't commit the citation-precision overclaim the tool is built to catch.

verdicts.verdict: From my lens — runaway loops, token spend, destructive actions, security — this is the strongest spec I'd expect from someone who actually got burned: the loop is genuinely bounded, the default path is network-free / LLM-free / fail-open, off-by-default, and the only hard gate is irreversible-data-loss downgraded to ASK not DENY. That is the right posture and it directly answers the $100/2-day burn and the no-Claude-at-runtime rule. I am NOT blocking on the cost/loop axis. BUT two things must be fixed before proceeding. (1) The credibility anchor is materially overclaimed: the spec repeatedly says the kernel is 'lifted directly from' a 'LIVE, battle-tested demote()' with signature gradeConfidence({distinctDomains, sourceAgeMonths, isProjection, humanReviewed}) and 'distinct-DOMAIN dedupe per engine-light.ts:303'. Also a self-inflicted DoS / latency multiplier the cost lens cares about.

defects.issue: guard-destructive.sh does regex shape-matching on the top-level Bash command string, but the honest-limitations section admits script-wrapped/variable-expanded targets are invisible. The spec frames this as 'escalate to ask' but a command whose destructive nature is hidden won't MATCH the regex at all, so it is silently ALLOWED, not escalated.
defects.fix: Add a coarse catch-all: any Bash invocation that itself spawns a shell/interpreter (bash -c, sh -c, eval, xargs, find -exec, env with reassignment) or contains command substitution should ALSO route to 'ask'.
